problem: NaVid's reliance on temporal visual history has not been systematically studied, and VLN models are rarely deployed on physical legged robots, so it is unclear how much history the model needs or whether it transfers to a quadruped.
motivation: Video-based VLN models such as NaVid encode past frames as memory, but the value of that memory at inference time is not quantified. Real-world legged deployment with only monocular RGB would show whether simulation-trained VLN can be executed on physical platforms without depth or retraining.
key_idea: Ablate the number of history frames NaVid sees at inference on R2R-CE val-unseen, and deploy the unmodified model on a Unitree Go2 quadruped using monocular RGB.
insight: NaVid's success rate rises monotonically with history length (9.4% with no history to 39.1% with full history). SPL is non-monotonic, with a threshold effect between 5 and 20 frames and a large jump from 20 frames to full history, so path efficiency needs long context while success improves gradually. The Go2 deployment shows the pipeline can produce executable behaviour on a legged robot without retraining.
method: History ablation: five inference-time conditions on NaVid (no history, 3, 5, 20 frames, full history) evaluated on R2R val-unseen in VLN-CE
Common subset evaluation: all conditions compared on a shared 617-episode subset of val-unseen
Sim-to-real deployment: unmodified NaVid runs on a Unitree Go2 quadruped using only monocular RGB
Controlled indoor trials: the deployment is tested under controlled indoor conditions, with no depth sensors, architectural changes or retraining

setting.backbone: NaVid (video-based VLM, pretrained, used without retraining)
setting.training_data: none additional (uses pretrained NaVid; only inference-time history varied)
setting.observation: monocular RGB video with history frames
setting.action_space: low-level continuous-control VLN actions (VLN-CE style) executed on a quadruped
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE) for the ablation; real Unitree Go2 for deployment

numbers_note: Abstract only. The abstract gives only SR 9.4% (no history) and 39.1% (full history); the SPL values are not given, and the 3/5/20-frame values are missing.
results: On a 617-episode R2R val-unseen subset, SR rises monotonically from 9.4% (no history) to 39.1% (full history). SPL is non-monotonic, with a threshold between 5 and 20 frames and a marked jump from 20 frames to full history. NaVid also produced executable navigation on a Unitree Go2 with monocular RGB and no retraining.
limitations: Small-scale thesis study, evaluated on a 617-episode subset, with only controlled indoor real-world tests
Only NaVid is analysed, and no quantitative real-robot metrics are given in the abstract
compares_to: NaVid history variants (no history, 3, 5, 20 frames, full history)
